clue.text: Stitched up, like this puzzle?

definitions.meaning: to stitch someone up is to betray or frame them, which is to double-cross them
a crossword's grid is crossed by answers both across and down, so it is jokingly crossed twice over

explanation.surface: A solver grumbles that they have been tricked, just as this crossword tricks them.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stitched up means being betrayed by someone you trusted; a crossword is literally crossed in two directions.

clue.text: Like Derby, plainly?

definitions.meaning: the Derby is a flat race, run without jumps
a plain is flat land, so being on the plain is being on level ground

explanation.surface: A racing pundit simply describes the famous English horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat racing has no fences, and a plain is a level tract of ground.

clue.text: Boat is exposed, shipping gallons

indicators.note: shipping means taking on board, so the other letter goes inside

parts.note: to be bare is to be exposed or uncovered

explanation.surface: A boat lies open to the weather, taking on gallons of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A barge is a flat-bottomed cargo vessel used on canals and rivers.

clue.text: Provider of polish, a grotesque comedian?

definitions.meaning: ... is an abrasive used for smoothing and polishing, as on an ... board
Dick ... was a British TV comedian known for outlandish characters

explanation.surface: A comic is described as grotesque but gives a fine polish to his act.
explanation.walkthrough: Dick Emery was a British TV comedian of the 1960s and 1970s, famous for grotesque character sketches.
explanation.definitionFit: Emery is a rough mineral powder used to buff and smooth surfaces, as nail files do.

clue.text: Kicks given no censure surprisingly

indicators.note: something surprising is unexpected, so the letters come out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A footballer's violent kicks go unpunished, to everyone's surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kicks' suggests football but is the sense of kicking a habit.
explanation.definitionFit: To kick a habit is to give it up, which is what renouncing it means.

clue.text: Seek arrest possibly for them (bit of exhibitionism unwanted?)

definitions.text: Seek arrest possibly for them (bit of exhibitionism unwanted?)

indicators.note: possibly says these letters might be arranged some other way
what is unwanted is thrown out of the letters
a bit of a word is here its first letter

explanation.surface: People who run naked in public all but ask to be arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges SEEK ARREST, and 'unwanted' then drops one E, the first letter of 'exhibitionism'. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Streakers run naked through public places, an exhibitionist act that can lead to arrest.

clue.text: Choice of letter size for keyboarder

definitions.meaning: choice as an adjective means select or best
a typewriter type size giving twelve characters to the inch

explanation.surface: A typist picks a font size.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are the select few, and elite was a standard typewriter typeface size.

clue.text: Feature of the gods not being concerned with supposedly lesser mortals?

definitions.text: Feature of the gods not being concerned with supposedly lesser mortals?

parts.words: Feature of the gods not being concerned with supposedly lesser mortals?
parts.note: self-absorbed beings who think only of themselves and ignore those beneath them show this trait

explanation.surface: Mythological deities are indifferent to the humans below them.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-centredness is the quality of caring only about oneself and disregarding others.

clue.text: Desert region has near waters diverted

indicators.note: waters that are diverted take another course, so the letters are rerouted

explanation.surface: A desert region lies close to waters that have been rerouted.
explanation.definitionFit: Western Sahara is a disputed desert territory on Africa's Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Singer Woody gets naughtier, leading couple stripping off

indicators.note: gets here means becomes, so the remaining letters turn into something new and are rearranged
the leading couple are the first two letters of the word, and stripping off says they are removed

explanation.surface: A folk singer is said to be misbehaving more and more, with a couple leading a striptease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading couple stripping off' takes NA from the front of NAUGHTIER, leaving UGHTIER, and 'gets' signals that those letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Woody Guthrie was the American folk singer behind This Land Is Your Land.

clue.text: Queen Victoria's beginning to interrupt all her children, quelling excitement?

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into, so these letters sit inside the other piece

parts.note: Queen Victoria had nine children, so all of them number NINE
ER is the usual abbreviation for a queen, from Elizabeth Regina

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only the start of the name is used

explanation.surface: Queen Victoria wades in among her own brood to calm them down.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue keeps Victoria in view, so 'all her children' means her family of nine.
explanation.definitionFit: A nervine is a medicine that soothes the nerves, so it acts by calming agitation.

clue.text: Make a fuss to avoid a Greek island

indicators.note: avoiding the letter means leaving it out of the word

parts.note: to create is informal British for making a fuss or a scene

explanation.surface: Someone tries not to cause a scene while visiting a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to avoid' drops the A from CREATE, British slang for kicking up a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Crete is the largest of the Greek islands, in the southern Aegean.

clue.text: Whatever suggestion that was given to Adam when new animal appeared?

definitions.meaning: the phrase means any thing at all, whichever you like to mention

definitions.text: suggestion that was given to Adam when new animal appeared?
definitions.meaning: in Genesis Adam named every animal, so he would be told to name it

explanation.surface: A light-hearted picture of God inviting Adam to name each new creature in Eden.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used to mean anything and everything, much like 'any you care to mention'.

clue.text: Riverside resident in provincial group

parts.note: NI is Northern Ireland, often called the Province
a lot is a group or set of things

explanation.surface: Someone living by a river belongs to a group out in the provinces.
explanation.walkthrough: Northern Ireland is often called the Province, which is how 'provincial' gives NI.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nilot is a member of a people living along the Nile valley.

clue.text: Statesman sees Libya torn apart

indicators.note: torn apart means pulled into pieces, so the letters are scattered and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A political leader looks on as Libya is ripped apart by conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Blair was British Prime Minister from 1997 to 2007, a leading politician.

clue.text: See list that includes one regarded as a revolutionary hero

indicators.note: including something means holding it inside

parts.note: a roster is a list, especially of duties

parts.words: one regarded as a revolutionary hero
parts.note: Che Guevara is widely regarded as a revolutionary hero

explanation.surface: Someone is told to check a list for a revolutionary icon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a command but is the definition: a see is a bishop's diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: Rochester is an English cathedral city and the seat of a bishop, so it is a diocese.

clue.text: People coming back see as a result of this instruction?

parts.words: see as a result of this instruction?
parts.note: read as an order, the answer tells you to turn the letters after it backwards, and doing so produces 'see'

explanation.surface: Travellers come home after being told what to see.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as RETURN EES: obeying that instruction turns EES round into SEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Returnees are those who come home after time away, such as returning emigrants.

clue.text: Native attempts to trap British on island

indicators.note: trapping something holds it inside

parts.note: tries are attempts
Man is the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A local tries to capture a Briton on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribesman is a member of a tribe, an indigenous inhabitant of a place.

clue.text: Restriction coming over time — it is an eye problem

indicators.note: the restriction comes over, covering the time, so it goes around it

parts.note: a rein is a restraint or check

explanation.surface: A doctor explains that a pressing restriction has turned into an eye complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Retinitis is inflammation of the retina, a medical condition of the eye.

clue.text: Aboard ship hurry to provide launches

indicators.note: being aboard means being on a ship, so these letters go inside the vessel's

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
hie is an old word for hurry

explanation.surface: Crew rush about on deck to get boats away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'launches' looks like boats but is a verb: to shy is to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: To shy something is to toss or fling it, the way a launch sends something flying.

clue.text: Bishop falling into lake in African country like a shot?

indicators.note: placed in the country means inside its letters

parts.note: Chad is a country in central Africa

indicators.note: falling into the lake puts the letter inside it

parts.note: a mere is a lake
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A clergyman tumbles into a lake in Africa as fast as a shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like a shot' suggests speed but means a round loaded in a gun's chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot or cartridge that is chambered has been loaded into the firing chamber of a gun.

clue.text: Overlooking North American lake is a nest

indicators.note: in a down clue overlooking means sitting above, so this letter comes first

parts.note: Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A bird's nest is perched high above one of the Great Lakes.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerie is an eagle's or other bird of prey's lofty nest.

clue.text: How one may lie in party game, stutteringly

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: a stutter repeats the opening sound of a word

parts.note: go is a Japanese board game

explanation.surface: Someone plays a party game while stammering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stutteringly' doubles the G at the start of GO, the board game.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie doggo is an idiom for keeping still and hidden, out of sight.

clue.text: European report of border activity?

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is spoken

parts.note: a check of passports is what happens at a frontier

explanation.surface: A news item describes goings-on at a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: A Czech is a native of the Czech Republic in central Europe.

clue.text: Cold climb posing problem for athlete?

parts.note: C stands for cold, as on taps
a ramp is a slope or climb

explanation.surface: A chilly uphill route causes difficulty for a runner.
explanation.definitionFit: A cramp is a painful muscle spasm that can stop a sportsperson mid-race.

clue.text: Row in world of Roman Church

parts.note: terra is the Latin, the Romans' word, for earth or world
CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: A dispute breaks out within the Roman Catholic world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel but it is a line of houses.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrace is a row of joined houses, the standard British street form.

clue.text: School physics unit facing ruin

parts.note: the gram is a unit of mass in physics
to mar is to spoil or ruin

explanation.surface: A school's physics department faces closure.
explanation.walkthrough: A grammar school is a British selective secondary school.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar is short for grammar school, a type of British secondary school.

clue.text: Very exciting Scottish team — super!

parts.note: Hearts is Heart of Midlothian, an Edinburgh football club
topping is old British slang for excellent

explanation.surface: A fan raves about an Edinburgh football club's thrilling form.
explanation.walkthrough: Hearts is the Edinburgh football club Heart of Midlothian.
explanation.definitionFit: Something heart-stopping is so thrilling it seems to make the heart pause.
